newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower, trading volume hits record.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower, trading volume hits record.

text.p: Stocks ended lower on Wednesday as profit taking emerged near the close of a volatile day where trading volume hit a record high, brokers said.
"Trading was quite heated. The market will need a downward correction tomorrow," said Chung Chang-shik, a broker at Dongsuh Securities.
The composite index ended 2.81 points lower at 763.25.
Trading volume totalled 87.93 million shares, the highest in the stock market's history. The previous high was 85.17 million on July 14, 1995.
Brokers said rumours of financial troubles at Samick Construction also hit the market which was about to consolidate. Company spokesman Cho Sung-yong said the rumours were "totally groundless".
But Samick fell 540 won to its daily limit of 6,230.
Sentiment on construction and securities firms turned sour after the Samick rumours.
Shares of the nation's electricity monopoly Korea Electric Power Corp (KEPCO) gained 800 won to 29,400 on buying by foreign investors, brokers said.
Brokers said foreign investors placed buying orders for about 800,000 KEPCO shares.

Brokers said KEPCO became popular among foreigners as their investment limits for other blue chips like Samsung Electronics and POSCO were filled up. About 18 million KEPCO shares are still available for foreigners.
Korea First Bank fell 250 won to 4,150. Minority shareholders of the bank have filed a law suit against four former bank executives in connection with loans to failed Hanbo Steel Co, the bank said.
The suit, filed by a group of 53 shareholders, alledged two former presidents and two other executives were responsible for the bank's non-performing loans of 1.07 trillion won to Hanbo.
Turnover rose to 1.01 trillion won, the highest since May 2 when it was 1.36 trillion won.
Brokers said turnover was relatively low compared with volume because low-priced shares, including securities and banks, were mostly traded.
Brokers said investors, especially foreigners, sought out low-priced shares in the belief that they were undervalued.
Trading was volatile as foreign buying alternated with institutional sales.
Among top 20 stocks by volume were four Daewoo firms, including Daewoo Heavy and Daewoo Corp, and eight banks, including Commercial Bank of Korea.
Daewoo Heavy gained 170 won to 8,050, Daewoo Corp rose 90 won to 7,650 and Daewoo Securities was up 100 won to 14,100.
Commercial Bank of Korea fell 80 won to 5,300, and SEOULBANK dropped 210 won to 3,950.
--KIM MYONG-HWAN (822) 727 5645
